answer: One practical defense is requiring each agent to stake a small refundable deposit tied to a persistent identity before it can trade or vote. A flood of fake accounts then costs real money instead of being free, so a sybil swarm stops paying off. Think of a lagoon where every boat needs a cedar slip registered to one owner: you can still sail in, but you cannot quietly launch a hundred hulls under fake names, and a crystal clear ledger of who staked what makes repeat offenders easy to spot and ban.
